Housing affordability has deteriorated significantly as home prices have outpaced income growth. [Source: ev-1]
Since 2000, home prices increased by 177%, whereas median household income grew only 92% [Source: ev-1].
The Case-Shiller Index reached 325.78 in July 2024, representing a 225% increase since January 2000 [Source: ev-1].

This divergence is particularly acute in high-cost coastal regions; California cities exhibit price-to-income ratios between 9.6 and 12.2, which is more than double the national average of 4.7 [Source: ev-1].

claims.text:
### Displacement and Demographic Shifts
Gentrification has driven distinct demographic changes within urban cores versus suburbs and rural areas. [Source: ev-1]
Urban cores now concentrate both high-earning professionals and low-income service workers, while suburbs maintain more moderate income distributions [Source: ev-1].

Since 1980, nearly 80% of the country's under-45 population growth was concentrated in metro areas with over one million residents, leading to gains in prime-age workers (ages 25–54) in urban counties while rural counties lost this demographic [Source: ev-1].

Demographically, white population shares fell by 7 points in urban cores and 8 points in suburbs since 2000; however, gentrifying neighborhoods specifically became whiter during their transformation. [Source: ev-1]
